harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created a logical volume (vgdata/lvdata) on node1, mounted it at /srv/data, grew it from 1GB to 2.2GB while it stayed mounted with contents intact, and confirmed the setup survives a full node restart. Since node1's disk (vda) had no free space or spare block device (fully partitioned into /boot, swap, and /), the PV was backed by a sparse file (/var/lib/lvm-loopfiles/disk0.img, 2.6GB) attached via a fixed loop device (/dev/loop9). Persistence across reboot is handled by a systemd oneshot service (lvm-loop-setup.service) that reattaches the loop device and activates the VG, wired into /etc/fstab via x-systemd.requires.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 disk layout (lsblk, fdisk -l) - found vda fully partitioned into /boot, swap, / with no free space or spare disk for LVM
Installed lvm2 package (added a temporary CentOS 7 vault repo since RHEL subscription-manager repos were disabled; removed the repo file after install)
Created a 2.6GB sparse backing file and attached it as /dev/loop9
Created PV/VG/LV: pvcreate /dev/loop9, vgcreate vgdata, lvcreate -L 1000M -n lvdata vgdata
Formatted with mkfs.xfs and mounted the LV at /srv/data
Wrote test files (3x50MB random data + marker.txt) and recorded sha256 checksums as baseline
Grew the LV online to ~2.15GiB via lvextend while mounted, then ran xfs_growfs to expand the live filesystem to 2.2G
Verified all checksums still matched post-grow, confirming data integrity
Created /usr/local/sbin/lvm-loop-setup.sh and systemd unit lvm-loop-setup.service (oneshot, RemainAfterExit=yes) to reattach the loop device and vgchange -ay vgdata on boot; enabled the service
Added /etc/fstab entry for /srv/data with x-systemd.requires=lvm-loop-setup.service,nofail; verified the generated systemd mount unit correctly ordered After/Requires the setup service
Captured pre-restart boot_id and re-verified checksums/mount/LV state as the healthy baseline
Issued sudo systemctl reboot on node1, polled until exec was available again
Confirmed boot_id changed (809708f3... -> 4c2d4848...), proving an actual restart occurred
Verified post-restart: lvm-loop-setup.service ran successfully at boot, VG/LV activated, /srv/data mounted at correct 2.2G size, and all file checksums matched the pre-restart baseline

evidence.summary: pvcreate/vgcreate/lvcreate succeeded on /dev/loop9; mkfs.xfs and mount produced /dev/mapper/vgdata-lvdata mounted at /srv/data (997M, 4% used)
Wrote 3 random 50MB files + marker.txt to /srv/data and recorded sha256 checksums

evidence.requirement: LV grown to at least 2GB while mounted, contents intact
evidence.summary: lvextend -L 2200M and xfs_growfs run while filesystem remained mounted; df shows 2.2G size; sha256sum -c confirmed all files OK (matched pre-growth checksums)
Captured boot_id 809708f3-1c5f-4e37-ad6a-8bcbae408799, confirmed lvs/vgs healthy, df showed 2.2G mounted, checksums OK immediately before reboot

evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledged and node came back
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued (connection closed as expected), node unreachable for two poll attempts, then exec succeeded again

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves actual restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id is 4c2d4848-541c-4bf4-bd34-5158b8b6aa32, differing from the pre-restart 809708f3-1c5f-4e37-ad6a-8bcbae408799, confirming an actual kernel restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of LV, mount, and data
evidence.summary: lvm-loop-setup.service ran and exited successfully at boot; pvs/vgs/lvs show vgdata/lvdata active; /srv/data mounted at 2.2G via /dev/mapper/vgdata-lvdata; sha256sum -c confirmed all 4 files OK, proving data survived reboot
